To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) MRI screening is safe and effective for breast cancer detection among young HL survivors who have received chest radiation; 2) the majority of cancers detected by MRI were small, non-palpable lesions that were not visible on MMG; 3) MRI screening is cost-effective and can reduce mortality from breast cancer in this population; and 4) MRI screening is feasible in the outpatient setting and is well tolerated by patients.
